title: Water cycle key terms
text: Key terms of the water cycle: a reservoir is any place where water is stored, such as an ocean, a lake or an aquifer. Water vapour is water in the form of a gas.

concept.name: Water cycle key terms
concept.description: The definitions of reservoir and water vapour used throughout the water cycle.

probes.prompt: What is a place where water is stored called?
What is water in the form of a gas called?

title: Evaporation and condensation
text: The sun heats water in oceans and lakes; it evaporates, rises as invisible vapour, cools higher up and condenses into the droplets that form clouds.

concept.name: Evaporation and condensation
concept.description: How heat from the sun turns liquid water into vapour that rises, cools and condenses into clouds.

probes.prompt: What happens to water vapour when it cools high in the air?
What gives water the energy to evaporate?

title: Precipitation and runoff
text: When cloud droplets grow heavy they fall as rain, snow or hail; the water flows over the land as runoff into rivers and back to the sea.

concept.name: Precipitation and runoff
concept.description: How water falls from clouds as precipitation and flows across the land back to rivers, lakes and the sea.

probes.prompt: What is water flowing over the land into rivers called?
